attribution.note: Zitron's own analytic statement in his newsletter, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Unhedged causal claim that more issuance raises the cost of the debt. The normalised text leaves out his two mechanisms (competition, investor risk), but it keeps the core causal commitment.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a market tendency measured by spreads over government debt is fair and ordinary. Treating hyperscaler AI bonds as AI data center debt is a reasonable plain reading. The result depends on the spread-vs-yield choice and on that universe.

evidence.note: PIMCO, data as of Sept 23, 2026, inside the window. Government-adjusted spreads with non-AI comparison: hyperscaler spreads widened as the market absorbed AI supply.
JPM, Sept 2026, calls the widening technical (supply-driven), not fundamental. That supports issuance raising cost, though it rejects reading more debt as more default risk.
July 16, 2026, before the window. Shows supply-driven widening on jumbo deals, which later stabilises. Background only.

reviews.rationale: Within the window, PIMCO and JPM both tie wider AI-borrower spreads to issuance volume, after adjusting for government rates, non-AI benchmarks and credit fundamentals. That supports the core claim. JPM disputes that more debt means weaker credit, but the claim's risk wording is ambiguous and the contract treats concentration risk separately. That part is not quantified and does not overturn the supply effect.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Firm conditional ('everybody suffers'). The antecedent (labs miss the revenue their valuations assume, ~$190–200B within two years for Anthropic) is kept, and so are the three named consequences.

contract.note: Reasonable plain reading: material harm to the three named groups, with the two-year deadline tied to the revenue condition. The ambiguities (OpenAI threshold, consequence lag) are flagged openly.

evidence.note: Aug 2026 TheStreet piece. Describes the $190–200B figure as a 2028 projection. Says nothing about whether the antecedent occurred or about any consequence.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent's deadline (Sept 2028) is after the evaluation date, and the early-resolution rule has not been met. Whether the antecedent holds is unknown, so the conditional cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own calculation, stated in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Firm counterfactual figure. The 'strictly cash basis' and 'if issued today' qualifiers are kept, and the September/November scope conflict is noted.

contract.note: Using the $18B September 2025 issue, priced at Sept 29, 2026 yields, as undiscounted extra lifetime interest is a fair reading of his flat calculation. The tenor convention is flagged.

evidence.note: Oracle prospectus copy: six tranches, $18B, 4.45%–6.10% coupons. Gives the original terms but no Sept 29, 2026 replacement yields.

reviews.rationale: Only the original bond terms were verified. No independent tranche-level yields for Sept 29, 2026 are in the packet, so the $6.89B total can be neither reproduced nor refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement in his newsletter, citing his earlier piece.

semantics.note: The normalised text keeps 'it appears' and a wide range ('anywhere from'). That is an evidential hedge expressing graded confidence, not a firm assertion of the figure.

contract.note: The contract applies a plain reading and scores a hedged ('it appears') estimate as if it were firm. Policy reserves plain-reading scoring for firm language.

evidence.note: Nov 2025 report of Nadella saying Microsoft has chips it cannot plug in. No dollar value, and it predates the target period.
Sept 2026 report on a forward-looking Morgan Stanley power-shortfall model. Not a measurement of idle GPUs already sold.

reviews.rationale: The figure is offered with 'it appears' and a broad range: hedged, graded confidence that policy does not score. Even setting the hedge aside, the packet has no independent estimate of idle NVIDIA inventory value, so nothing would settle it.
